extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of classical Euclidean geometry (readers of historical Italian geometry texts)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures for classifying and computing areas and lengths in quadrilaterals (rhombi, rhomboids, and other types) using diagonals, decomposition into triangles, proportionality, powers (squares), roots, and arithmetic manipulation. The text gives stepwise measurement algorithms and classification criteria in old Italian.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area of a rhombus via its diagonals
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules about multiplying the diagonals of a rhombus to obtain its area: e.g. “eglie vno rombo... multiplicato vn Diametro in Cete laltro ... elareae...aditnado$toe ciafeu^ no Diametro... larea del róbo” and related passages that multiply one diameter by the other and take halves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the area of a rhombus from its diagonals by multiplying the two diagonals and applying the appropriate division (half) depending on which parts are taken — i.e. the classical rule that the area of a rhombus equals (d1 * d2) / 2. The text gives variants using half/whole diagonals and explains when to take halves to get the correct area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area relationships using half-diagonals and proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures that use halves (mita) of diagonals and multiplication to obtain areas: e.g. “la mita de Idiametro..., la mita del uno adonca perverà 1 2 o.cioe a  meare la mita du diametro g tutto laltro fara. 1 2 o,£l qìc e larea di robo.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When only half-diagonals or parts of diagonals are used, multiply the appropriate half by the other diagonal (or its half) and divide as indicated to obtain the desired area proportion (half-area, quarter-area, etc.). The chapter explains how multiplying halves yields half or quarter of the full product and thus the corresponding fraction of the area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area of a rhomboid (parallelogram) via base and height (catetto × bafa)
rubrics_metrics.description: For romboide (parallelogram) the area is obtained by multiplying an appropriate catetto (height) by the base (bafa): “larea 01 tutto il romboide... il catetto... nel triangolo... la bafa... multiplicarai d catetto.a e.p la bafa.b c.e barai larea 01 tutto il romboide.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert the parallelogram to triangles (by a diagonal) and compute area via base × height; equivalently, area(romboide) = base × altitude. Text demonstrates doing this by forming corresponding triangles and multiplying the catetto (perpendicular) by the base (bafa).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decompose quadrilateral into triangles to compute area
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeatedly the text instructs to divide the quadrilateral by a diameter (diagonal) into two triangles and use the areas of these triangles to get the area of the quadrilateral: e.g. “per lo Diametro per lo quale la oitta figura fia oiuifa in 2 triangoli iguali... per lo Diametro fuo multiplicaremo e baremo la rea 01 tutto il romboide.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw diagonals to split a quadrilateral into triangles; compute each triangle's area (using base × height or other triangle rules) and sum them to obtain the quadrilateral's area. Many measurement procedures in the text reduce quadrilateral measurement to triangle measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of powers (squares) and roots in area computations and commensurability handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The text prescribes multiplying lines by appropriate powers and taking roots when diameters are not commensurable or to change magnitudes: e.g. “per lo magi02C lato la radici... il lato magt02C... moltiplica adoca vna cofa... del quale la radia e il lato mmo2C. £ p ebe eglie eofi.a.al,b.cofi.o.3l.e.fara adoca com ino il quadrato...” and passages about multiplying by 9, 64, 169 etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When dealing with irrational or incommensurable lengths (diameters), the text shows multiplying by integer powers (squares, fourths etc.) to obtain numbers whose squares or roots can be taken arithmetically; then divide back by the same powers. This is an algorithmic rationalization to permit arithmetic computation of lengths and areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification criteria for quadrilaterals (species definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed taxonomy of quadrilaterals by equality/equidistance of sides and nature of angles (caput abscissum, capo tagliato, capo inclinante, etc.): e.g. “Huidefe qucUoquaito genere Degli quadrilateri... gli primi fi Dicono caput abfcifura... quelli che hano c.2 .ladoppoSli equcdiUand e non iguali... il lato.a b.fe ©ieicapo tagliatore... capo tagliato... capo inclinante...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the given morphological criteria (which sides are equal, which are equidistant, whether angles at the head are right/acute/obtuse, whether a corner is cut or inclined) to classify a quadrilateral into the named species; classification then determines the preferred measurement method in later chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measuring quadrilaterals with a ‘capo tagliato’ (cut/truncated corner)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific rules for quadrilaterals where the head (capo) is cut: e.g. “quanto al mode di mifurar le figure quadrilatere le quali fi dicono caput abfcifum... e seguendo diremo de la feconda fpecie... capo tagliato... la quale il lato*a d.cioe il capo ecquedillàte ala bafa...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a quadrilateral with a corner cut, measure by relating the cut portions (capo and bafa) to triangle bases and catetti; the text prescribes multiplying and dividing by halves of sides and using the catetto on the point of cut to compute the area (effectively decomposing into triangles and applying proportional rules).

rubrics_metrics.guidance: When two configurations are proportional, area computations (multiplications yielding areas) can be transferred by exchanging proportional factors. The manual shows how permuting proportional factors produces equivalent area expressions and thus how to compute unknown areas from known proportional relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive procedures when diagonals intersect (interfegano) to produce calculable triangles
rubrics_metrics.description: When diagonals/lines intersect, form auxiliary lines and points so that intersecting diameters produce triangles whose catetti and bases can be used multiplicatively: e.g. “H fe il ponto Doue finterfega tali Diametri voi bauei’C.Bgiongni el capo con la bafa ficnno.26.cbe in fe multiphea fienno.ó76.£ Dipoi irc3po.a b.in fe multipli ca:doe.8.fanno.64.£”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce intersection points of diagonals and draw perpendiculars/catetti to create triangles with known proportional relations. Then apply repeated multiplications/divisions (possibly by factors like 26, 64, 324 etc. as the text exemplifies) to reduce to manageable numbers and extract roots to find lengths and areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic reduction to avoid overly large multiplications (factoring out common parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice on avoiding excessively large multiplicative intermediate numbers by factoring and dividing during multiplication and division steps: e.g. “modo del troppo gràde multiplicaméto e partitimento... togli nnino2Ì numeri la medefima ^jpojtione e barai la medefima mulnplicatióe e dimTione... certame/ te.5’8o.a.64.cómo il quarto di.f 8o.al quarto de.é4.doe”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When intermediate multiplications would produce unwieldy large numbers, reduce by dividing common factors at intermediate stages (i.e., cancel factors before multiplying) so that the same proportion/multiplication is preserved but numbers remain manageable; the text gives examples using 9, 64, 169, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement by carrying a line from a vertex until lines meet (constructive measurement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for drawing a line from a given vertex/edge until lines meet a point and then computing lengths/areas from the resultant configuration: e.g. “voi menare dafeuna de le linee.a b.e.c d.p lo diritto infino fi congmngino i ficmi nel ponto.ì... noi babiamo ditto cbe.a d.e.i 2 .e.b c,e. i 6.adoca...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extend/draw lines from a given side or vertex until they intersect a target point; use the resulting triangles and proportional relations to calculate desired segment lengths or areas, following the decomposition-into-triangles strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules relating squares of lines (powers) to area computations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of squares of segment lengths in deriving area relations and reconstructing diameters: e.g. many passages with statements like “il quadrato de la linea... il quadrato del diametro... la radice de...”, and operations multiplying and dividing by squares (9, 169, 324...) to find line magnitudes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute areas or reconstruct lengths by forming squares (powers) of appropriate segments; when needed, take square roots to return to line measures. The text demonstrates how to manipulate squares and their roots arithmetically to transit between lengths and areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for quadrilaterals with unequal but equidistant sides (symmetry/equidistance rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for measuring quadrilaterals where opposite sides are equidistant but not equal; such figures are reduced to the base species and measured by the same multiplication/division of catetti and bafa: e.g. “Le quadrilateri non baranno ilati equediftantitaoc ebe ninno efe lati fia equcdi dante alaltro...” and subsequent measurement steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If opposite sides are equidistant (parallels) but unequal in length, treat the figure as a romboide/parallelogram and apply the usual base × height or triangle-decomposition techniques; the text explains how to reduce many such cases to previously treated ones.
